acf.category_faq:
How do I size high bay wattage? | Start with lux target, mounting height and aisle width; efficacy then determines the required wattage.
Which protection rating is suitable? | IP65 covers most industrial dust and moisture; IP69K is used for high-pressure washdown areas.
Can controls be grouped by zone? | Yes, DALI and 0-10V options can be documented per aisle, bay or process zone.
Do you support project-based quantities? | Yes, quotations are prepared from project quantities, configurations and delivery windows.
acf.category_long_description:
Industrial lighting has to work around the real building: racking heights, aisle widths, process heat, dust, cold stores, maintenance access and operating hours. A specification that looks efficient on a datasheet can fail in practice if optics, controls and ingress protection do not match the installation.

How we engineer the range

We classify industrial products by mounting height, beam pattern, environmental protection and control strategy. For racking aisles, beam control and vertical illuminance are as important as floor lux. For process halls, maintenance access and driver quality become more important. For cold stores, low-temperature starting and sealed construction decide long-term reliability.

Documentation buyers receive

  • Product datasheets and installation guidance
  • IES / DIM photometric files where applicable
  • Declarations and market-specific certification support
  • Packing, loading and configuration summaries

When to involve our team

Send drawings early if the project includes high racking, temperature extremes, washdown zones, DALI grouping or tender-specific compliance. Early review reduces redesign and helps the quotation reflect the actual installation.

Designing for exterior conditions

Choosing the right interior range

Specify by cleaning zone

  • Conformity and test documentation

Providing these details with the enquiry helps ensure the selected product is suitable for both operation and inspection.

industries.title: Warehouse & Logistics Lighting
industries.excerpt: High bay layouts that cut fixture count in narrow racking aisles and survive 24/7 dock operation.
industries.content: We size high bay layouts from racking drawings, not generic spacing rules. Linear optics in aisles and UFO fittings at docks give the cleanest energy-per-lux result.

acf.challenge: Narrow racking aisles waste light from round high bays, while 24/7 dock operation punishes drivers that cannot handle frequent switching.
acf.outcome: A typical 10,000 m² retrofit reduces connected load by 55–65% and pays back in 14–24 months at European industrial tariffs.

industries.title: Parking & Exterior Area Lighting
industries.excerpt: Spill-light controlled floods and street fittings for car parks, yards and access roads.
industries.content: Car park and yard projects usually fail on spill light and glare complaints, not on lux numbers. We select asymmetric optics per pole position and verify beam edges against site boundaries.

acf.challenge: Open car parks need uniform ground lighting without throwing light into neighbouring residential windows.
acf.outcome: Asymmetric distributions keep boundary spill below EPL limits while cutting pole count on most sites.

industries.title: Retail & Supermarket Lighting
industries.excerpt: Low-glare panels and accent lighting that keep shelves bright without washing out displays.
industries.content: Retail lighting has two jobs: keep UGR below 19 for staff comfort, and keep colour consistent across fresh food zones. We combine panels for ambient light with high-CRI options where merchandising needs it.

acf.challenge: Open ceiling retail spaces mix office-style comfort requirements with food-zone colour rendering rules.
acf.outcome: Panel grids at 300–400 lux with targeted high-CRI zones keep both facilities managers and merchandisers satisfied.

guides.title: How to Choose LED High Bay Wattage
guides.excerpt: A four-step method for sizing high bay wattage from mounting height, lux targets and racking layout.
guides.content:
Start from lux, not wattage

Define the task first: 150–200 lux for storage, 300 lux for packing, 500 lux for fine assembly. Wattage is only a consequence of the required lumens and the fitting's efficacy.

Convert height to beam choice

Below 6 m use wide beams; 8–12 m suits 60°–90° UFO optics; above 12 m tighten the beam and raise wattage per fitting instead of adding fixtures.

Check the racking layout

In aisles narrower than 4 m, linear optics beat round fittings on uniformity and fixture count.

Validate the payback

Compare connected load and annual hours; most industrial retrofits pay back in under two years.

guides.title: IP Ratings Explained for Lighting Buyers
guides.excerpt: What IP65, IP66 and IP69K actually protect against, and which one your project needs.
guides.content:
The two digits

The first digit covers solids and dust, the second covers water. IP6x means dust-tight; the second digit scales from dripping water (3) to high-pressure jets (6) and washdown (9K).

Common mistakes

IP65 is not automatically better than IP66 for every project: IP66 focuses on heavy seas and jets, while IP69K adds close-range high-temperature washdown. Food plants should specify IP69K explicitly.

Match rating to location

Dry indoor: IP44. Covered outdoor: IP65. Open yard: IP66. Food processing and cold store washdown: IP69K.

guides.title: Export Certifications: CE, SAA and ETL
guides.excerpt: Which certifications European, Australian and North American buyers ask for, and how we document them.
guides.content:
Europe

CE marking covers EMC and LVD directives; ENEC is a voluntary quality mark that tender documents increasingly reference.

Australia and New Zealand

SAA approval is required for luminaires sold into Australia. We ship test reports with container documents to smooth customs checks.

North America

ETL or UL listing is the practical baseline, plus DLC listing where utility rebate programmes apply.

Documentation we provide

Every project ships with declarations of conformity, test reports and warranty terms in a single PDF pack.
